summary: The Prince's Court: the most populous southern crown, indebted to Postondoroth and courted by the Pact, with a short hill coast and the eastern end of the Gold Road.

blozans_household_spirit.name: Blozan's Household
blozans_household_spirit.desc: The prince's household fills a hill fortress with cooks, scribes and stewards, and every one of them listens at doors. Blozan knows what is said in his halls before it is finished.

prince_of_plutondo.name: The Prince of Plutondo
prince_of_plutondo.desc: Hill lords bow at the gate, desert lords at the hall and the Pact's envoys at the high seat. The prince is no longer one lord among many, and he has begun to dress as if he knew it.

hill_granaries.name: Granaries of the Hills
hill_granaries.desc: Stone granaries stand in every hill village, sealed with the prince's mark and filled before the first frost. A poor harvest in Plutondo means a thin winter, not a famine.

levy_rolls_spirit.name: The Levy Rolls
levy_rolls_spirit.desc: Every household has its name on the long scroll, and every name has its place in a company. The prince can call ten thousand in a week and feed them for a month.

pacts_right_hand.name: The Pact's Right Hand
pacts_right_hand.desc: Plutondo's spears ride beside Stabilo's in every drill and parade. The Pact's captains say the hill levies are the best-fed troops in the East.

boundary_stones.title: Between Drak and Erco
boundary_stones.desc: Boundary stones between the three crowns have moved again, and the shepherds on each side swear that the others moved them. The prince's surveyors have walked the line twice and found it a little different each time.

focuses.name: The Prince's Court
focuses.desc: Prince Blozan rules sixteen states of desert, hills and a short coast, and fills the caravans of the Gold Road with his porters and guards. Plutondo is crowded, poor and proud.

focuses.name: Blozan's Household
focuses.desc: The prince's household is large, loud and well informed. It holds the keys to every granary and the names of every debtor in the principality.

focuses.name: Lords of the Desert Hills
focuses.desc: The hill lords bring their riders in on the prince's call and take their share of the road-tolls in return. Their loyalty is bought every season, and so far it has held.

focuses.name: The Prince's Treasury
focuses.desc: A vaulted treasury with three locks takes the place of the old strongbox. The prince's clerks keep two ledgers, one for Postondoroth's eyes and one for their own.

focuses.name: Between Drak and Erco
focuses.desc: Plutondo lies between the sword-kingdom of Drak and the mountain kingdom of Erco, and both are touchy about the line. Blozan's surveyors have been asked to walk it once more.

focuses.name: The Prince of Plutondo
focuses.desc: The title is read aloud in the hill fortress, and the hill lords answer with one voice. The prince is now the first of Plutondo, not one of its many.

focuses.name: The Many of Plutondo
focuses.desc: Plutondo has more people than any other southern crown, and the prince counts them with pride. Porters, guards and ploughmen all answer to the muster.

focuses.name: Granaries of the Hills
focuses.desc: Stone granaries rise in every hill village, built by the people they feed. The prince's seal on the lintel promises a winter without hunger.

focuses.name: The Levy Rolls
focuses.desc: The rolls are rewritten each autumn, village by village. A man's name, trade and age are copied by two clerks, and the second copy goes to the prince.

focuses.name: Workshops of the Many
focuses.desc: Joiners, weavers and rope-makers set up in long sheds beside the caravan yards. They work cheaply, because there are always more hands.

focuses.name: Fields of Plutondo
focuses.desc: New terraces climb the hillsides, and canals bring snow-melt to dry fields. The yield is small per acre and large in total.

focuses.name: The Great Levy
focuses.desc: When the prince sounds the great horn, every village sends its companies to the hill fortress. A host of that size has not been seen in the East since the roads were opened.

focuses.name: Eastern Gate of the Gold Road
focuses.desc: The Gold Road reaches its eastern gate in Plutondo, and every cart that arrives has come through Postondoroth's hands. A paved court and a toll-house make the gate worth its name.

focuses.name: A Seat in the Pact
focuses.desc: Stabilo's Pact would welcome Plutondo, and Blozan's debts make the friendship easy. A seat at the Pact's table would also seat Postondoroth's bankers at his.

focuses.name: Pay Down the Ledger
focuses.desc: Blozan sets aside a fixed share of every toll for Postondoroth's clerks. The debt shrinks slowly, and with it the prince's need to flatter.

focuses.name: The Pact's Right Hand
focuses.desc: Plutondo's levies now stand at the Pact's right, and their captains drill beside Stabilo's veterans. The prince's name is read first at the Pact's table after the king's.

focuses.name: No Man's Debtor
focuses.desc: The last coin is paid, the last ledger closed, and the prince walks out of Postondoroth's counting-house a free man. His hill lords cheer in the streets.

focuses.name: The Gold Road's End
focuses.desc: Wagons unload in Plutondo's yards and the porters start their long walk home. The prince's market is the busiest of the eastern gates.

focuses.name: Caravan Porters
focuses.desc: Plutondo's porters carry the Gold Road's goods up the last steep miles, and the road-houses that feed them are said to be the best in the East. Postondoroth's factors pay a fair rate for such labour.

focuses.name: The Hill Coast
focuses.desc: The short coast under the hills has small bays and rough water. Fishermen have sailed it for generations, and the prince now wants the shipwrights to follow.

focuses.name: Galleys of the Hill Coast
focuses.desc: Oared galleys with high prows suit the coast's short chop. The yards at the capital's port turn them out in pairs.

focuses.name: Harbour of Plutondo
focuses.desc: A stone mole reaches into the bay, and warehouses crowd the quay behind it. Ships from the south now put in where the hills meet the water.

focuses.name: The Coastal Watch
focuses.desc: A tower is built on the headland and a beacon-keeper posted day and night. Smugglers have learned to sail by other coasts.

focuses.name: Sailors of Plutondo
focuses.desc: The coast's fishers and ferrymen are taken into the prince's service and taught to row in time. They are the first sailors Plutondo has ever had.
